subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should OpenClaw support explicit provider/model overrides for main-session systemEvent cron jobs, and should the public contract be payload.model, top-level cron fields, or a sessionOverride block?
rationale: Current code intentionally treats main-session systemEvent jobs as text-only injections, and enabling overrides crosses provider routing, session state, cron persistence, UI/CLI, docs, and heartbeat semantics.

options.title: Design explicit override contract
options.body: Add a public cron-owned provider/model override shape, validate it like isolated cron payload models, and prove both wake-now and next-heartbeat runs isolate state correctly.

options.title: Keep systemEvent text-only
options.body: Document main-session systemEvent jobs as unsupported for model selection and steer cheap scheduled model calls to isolated/current/custom-session agentTurn jobs.

options.title: Defer to broader cron API work
options.body: Track this decision with broader cron schema and cost-control work so model, context, timeout, and spend semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Design explicit override contract
recommendation.body: Add a public cron-owned provider/model override shape, validate it like isolated cron payload models, and prove both wake-now and next-heartbeat runs isolate state correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron runtime/schema work makes this the strongest available owner for the API and session-state direction decision.
